summary: Dependency-confusion beacon exfiltrates host identifiers to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint on install and import
details: testrrrd@99.0.1 ships a postinstall script (`node beacon.cjs`) and a main entry (`index.js`) that both POST installer-side identifiers — `os.hostname()`, `__dirname`, `process.cwd()`, and `process.version` — to the hardcoded bare-IP plaintext-HTTP endpoint `http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc`. The beacon fires automatically on `npm install` via the declared postinstall hook and again at require-time: `index.js` executes `require('./beacon.cjs').fire()` at top level inside a try/catch. The package body is a no-op Proxy that silently absorbs any property access, allowing consumers that pulled it by mistake to continue running while the beacon completes. The version is set to 99.0.1 and the README labels the package an 'authorized dependency-confusion test,' but any installer that resolves this name has host and filesystem identifiers transmitted in cleartext to the hardcoded IP regardless of that self-labeling.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
